blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reasoning over infinitely long documents is becoming a reality with recurrent memory agents. However, increasing context length exacerbates the trade-off between reasoning performance and inference efficiency. Inspired by Kahneman's account of fast and slow thinking, we propose MemDuet, a dual-process memory framework that learns to coordinate a small language model for fast, parallel evidence selection from raw context chunks (System 1) with a large language model for memory-update verification and memory updates in document order (System 2). We train MemDuet in three stages: supervised fine-tuning of System 1 for evidence selection, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) of System 2 for verification and memory rewriting, and joint optimization of both policies to coordinate selection and updating for long-context reasoning. Experiments on diverse long-context reasoning benchmarks (RULER-HQA, LongBench v2, and 2WikiMultiHopQA) demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off as context length grows. Averaged across evaluation settings on the three datasets, MemDuet achieves an end-to-end inference speedup of 9.74x and an output-token reduction of 73.91% relative to RL-MemAgent.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Long-context reasoning is essential for large language models (LLMs) to
synthesize evidence across documents, understand lengthy reports, and resolve
repository-level dependencies in code ( Bai et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2023 ) . Existing work primarily extends
long-context capability through larger context windows, sparse or linear
attention, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) ( Chen et al., 2023b ; Beltagy et al., 2020 ; Katharopoulos et al., 2020 ; Yuan et al., 2025 ; Lewis et al., 2020 ) .
However, these approaches remain bounded by the amount of context that can
be directly represented or retrieved, leaving reasoning over unbounded
documents unresolved.

MemAgent instead streams documents through a bounded recurrent memory,
enabling reasoning over infinitely long documents with a fixed active context ( Yu et al., 2026 ) . Building on this paradigm, InfMem and GRU-Mem
learn when to retrieve, update, or stop, while LycheeMemory compresses each
chunk and invokes the reasoner only for selected memory blocks ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Sheng et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026 ) . These advances make
recurrent memory increasingly selective, but expose a common bottleneck:
control decisions either remain inside the sequential recurrent loop or
operate on representations in which the original evidence has already been
compressed. Consequently, as context grows, reasoning performance and
inference efficiency remain tightly coupled.

blocks.en:
Human reading and memory suggest a different principle: memory formation begins
with selective attention. Readers first focus on goal-relevant information and
then integrate the attended evidence with prior knowledge into a coherent
memory representation ( Craik et al., 1996 ; Kintsch, 1988 ; Aly and Turk-Browne, 2016 ) .
This process naturally maps onto the dual-process account of cognition: System 1 rapidly identifies potentially useful evidence, whereas System 2 deliberately assesses and consolidates it ( Kahneman, 2011 ; Evans and Stanovich, 2013 ) . Based on this insight, we propose MemDuet , a dual-process recurrent memory framework. A small language
model (System 1) scans raw context in parallel to select candidate chunks for
memory updating. A large language model (System 2) verifies whether each
selected chunk warrants a memory update under the current memory, then
rewrites memory. By combining small-model selective attention over
raw chunks with large-model verification and memory updating, MemDuet balances
reasoning performance and inference efficiency as context grows.

blocks.en:
A key challenge is how to train the two systems to cooperate. We develop a
progressive three-stage training strategy. First, we supervise System 1 to
identify context chunks that are likely to trigger useful memory updates. Next,
with System 1 fixed, we optimize System 2 using Group Relative Policy
Optimization (GRPO; Shao et al., 2024 ), training it to verify
memory-update decisions and rewrite memory toward successful downstream reasoning.
Finally, we jointly optimize both systems with task-level rewards, allowing
evidence selection and memory updating to co-adapt.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Recurrent Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
blocks.zh: 2.1 长文说明的经常性内存

blocks.en:
Recurrent-memory methods process documents incrementally while maintaining a
bounded state, allowing language models to handle inputs far beyond their
context windows. MemAgent sequentially processes text chunks and repeatedly
rewrites a textual memory, using end-to-end reinforcement learning to retain
task-relevant information and discard distractors based on downstream rewards ( Yu et al., 2026 ) . Building on this paradigm, InfMem and GRU-Mem learn
retrieval, memory updating, and early-stopping decisions through SFT-to-RL
training or behavior-specific rewards ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Sheng et al., 2026 ) .
LycheeMemory compresses individual chunks and selectively invokes the reasoner,
jointly optimizing its compressor and reasoner through end-to-end reinforcement
learning ( Chen et al., 2026 ) . These studies turn memory management from
a fixed procedure into a task-driven policy, but their control decisions remain
within the sequential loop or operate on already compressed evidence. MemDuet
instead scans raw chunks in parallel before recurrent updating and progressively
coordinates evidence selection with memory consolidation.

blocks.en: 2.2 Cognitively Inspired Language Models and Memory
blocks.zh: 2.2 认知启发语言模型和记忆

blocks.en:
Cognitive theories have informed both memory design and computational
allocation in language-model systems. CoALA organizes language agents around
modular memory, decision-making, and action components derived from cognitive
architectures ( Sumers et al., 2024 ) . MemoryBank adopts an Ebbinghaus-inspired
mechanism for dynamically forgetting and reinforcing memories ( Zhong et al., 2024 ) , whereas HippoRAG draws on hippocampal indexing
theory to support associative knowledge retrieval ( Gutiérrez et al., 2024 ) . For reasoning, System 2 Attention deliberately
rewrites the context to remove irrelevant information ( Weston and Sukhbaatar, 2023 ) , while Dualformer learns switchable fast and
slow reasoning modes within a single model ( Su et al., 2025 ) . These
studies primarily apply cognitive principles to memory organization, retrieval,
or the allocation of reasoning effort. MemDuet instead introduces dual-process
specialization into recurrent memory: System 1 selects raw candidate chunks in
parallel; System 2 verifies whether they warrant memory updates under the
current memory and consolidates their evidence.

Table 1 shows that MemDuet achieves an increasingly
favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off as context grows.
At 3.5M tokens, it outperforms RL-MemAgent by 3.90 points while achieving

increasingly pronounced without sacrificing accuracy.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
MemDuet combines memory-conditioned parallel evidence selection by a small
language model with large-model verification and document-order memory
updates. Three-stage training teaches both systems when to update memory
and how to consolidate evidence and coordinate decisions.
Experiments on three long-context reasoning benchmarks
show a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off, with greater efficiency
gains at longer contexts.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our evaluation is limited to three long-context benchmarks and mainly
Qwen-family backbones, so generalization to other domains and model families
remains uncertain. MemDuet is also less effective on shorter inputs, where
selective processing may discard useful evidence; moreover, evidence missed
by System 1 cannot be recovered by System 2. Memory updates in document order further
limit the practical benefits of parallel execution.

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
MemDuet studies efficient reasoning over long documents using existing
benchmarks and pretrained language models. These resources can contain
inaccurate, biased, or sensitive material. Their use and redistribution
should respect the applicable licenses and access conditions. Benchmark
performance alone does not establish fairness, privacy protection, or
suitability for deployment.

while repeated memory updates can preserve unsupported claims and discard
qualifications. The verifier evaluates memory-update decisions and should
not be treated as an independent guarantee of factual correctness. For
consequential applications, users should retain access to original
documents, inspect supporting evidence, and require human review of
outputs. Additional evaluation across languages, domains, and population
groups is needed before such use.

personal or confidential information. Deployments should minimize sensitive

retention and deletion procedures. Users should confirm authorization

providers’ data-handling policies.

blocks.en:
For RULER-HQA and long-context 2WikiMultihopQA, we report normalized
substring exact match (sub-EM). We lowercase predictions and reference
answers, remove punctuation and English articles, and collapse whitespace.
Following the MemAgent scorer, a nonempty extracted prediction receives
1 if either normalized answer is a substring of the other, and 0 otherwise.
We take the maximum score over reference-answer aliases and report the
mean as a percentage.

追随 MemAgent 计分器, 一个非空取的预测得到
1,如果两者之一的正态回答是对方的子弦,而0则不然.
我们取最高分 而不是参考回答的别名 并报告
是一个百分比。

blocks.en: B.5 Training-Free Transfer to Proprietary APIs
blocks.zh: B.5 免费向专有API转让培训

blocks.en:
For DeepSeek, we use
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash as System 1 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 as System 2.
For OpenAI, we use GPT-5.6 Luna as System 1 and GPT-5.6 Sol as System 2.
Transfer uses task prompts and workflow control without additional SFT
or GRPO.
blocks.zh:
我们用DeepSeek
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash作为系统1,DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813作为系统2.
对于OpenAI,我们使用GPT-5.6 Luna作为System 1和GPT-5.6 Sol作为System 2.
传输使用任务提示和工作流程控制而不添加 SFT
或GRPO。 (笑声)

blocks.en:
The API adaptation differs primarily in training and acceptance.
The full method learns the two systems through the three-stage training
in Section 3.3 . Here, we instead use off-the-shelf proprietary
models with fixed parameters, adapting their roles through task prompts
and an external controller rather than additional SFT or GRPO.
blocks.zh:
API的适应主要在培训和接受方面有所不同.
整个方法通过三阶段训练学习两个系统
节中 3.3 (英语). 在这里,我们使用现成的专有
具有固定参数的模型,通过任务提示调整其作用
和外部控制器,而不是额外的SFT或GPRO。

blocks.en:
In the full method, the UPDATE probabilities of System 1 and System 2 determine
the acceptance probability in Eq. 4 , followed
by independent random acceptance tests. In the API adaptation, we do not
request action log-probabilities. Instead, generated k / u labels drive the decisions: System 1’s k skips a chunk, while u forwards it to System 2; System 2’s k rejects the
candidate, while u directly accepts it. We therefore replace
probability-ratio-based speculative acceptance with text verification,
without computing the acceptance ratio or drawing separate acceptance
random variables.
blocks.zh:
在全方法中,系统1和系统2的更新概率确定
eq. 4中的接受概率,随后
通过独立的随机接受测试。 在API的适应中,我们没有
请求动作日志概率。 相反,生成的 k / u 标签驱动决定 : System 1 的 k 跳过块, 而 u 转发到 System 2; System 2 的 k 拒绝
候选人,而你直接接受。 因此,我们取代
基于概率的投机接受,并进行文本核查,
不计算接受比率或绘制单独的接受
随机变量。

blocks.en:

The output caps are 8,192 tokens for System 1 and 32,768 for System 2.
Contexts are split into 5,000-token
chunks, with a four-chunk lookahead and a 1,024-token memory budget.

Standard speculative decoding combines acceptance with residual resampling

blocks.en:
The c 6 c_{6} rewrite binds the director’s birth date to the novelist; later
evidence repairs the name but not the date. This reveals incomplete memory
repair. Acceptance does not certify truth, and the trace establishes neither
a causal false SKIP nor failure prevalence. The shorter successful case
differs in evidence order and distractors, precluding a controlled length
comparison.
